purpose-and-scope.text: Singular is a permissionless registry on Cardano for unique identities and independent application state, built on an authenticated MPF map and representative NFTs. This specification covers registry operations, native requests, certification and custody, and selects no language, encoding, plugin, KERI integration or library API.

entities-and-terminology.text: The diagram shows the registry, whose map sends keys to Active or Over; the representative NFT; the Insert request UTxO carrying an application-minted action token and no NFT; the Update or Delete request UTxO carrying the existing representative; the configured application policy that mints action tokens; and the application spending script that holds the NFT and releases it into terminal requests.
The roles are semantically distinct even when scripts share a hash. The interface target is one parameter, the application policy ID.

required-behavior.text: Nine requirement sections follow. Must and must not express requirements of the intended protocol.

registry-transitions-and-representative-.text: The state diagram shows absent to Active on Insert with a mint into the certified output, Active to Over on Update with a burn, Active to absent on Delete with a burn, and Over as terminal.
Over has no live representative. Delete permits a later Insert. Active denotes an outstanding representative, including in a pending request, and carries no application payload.

native-request-construction.text: Insert and Withdraw use action tokens minted under the configured application policy, which enforces approval and construction at minting. The releasing application validator enforces binding and custody for Update and Delete requests. Singular's witnesses recompute the action-bound name and refuse substitute policies. Creating an output at the address is not admission. Request creation must not require observing the mutable registry.

insert-approval-at-request-minting.text: Minting an Insert token requires accepted certification of the exact proposal, binding registry, key, policy evidence, initial state, destination and output requirements. The policy ID is an authenticated parameter; no field is substitutable after approval; approval is established at minting and reserves nothing. Declared effects are explicit native output parameters, not a predicate language.

insert-pending-completion-and-withdrawal.text: A pending Insert holds no representative and asserts nothing about absence. Folding checks absence in the successive state and creates exactly the certified output atomically, refusing occupied keys. Withdrawal uses a separate Withdraw action token bound to the exact pending UTxO and refund terms, changes no registry state and mints nothing.

update-and-delete-application-authorizat.text: A terminal request carries the authentic representative for its exact registry and key. The application spending validator authorizes that exact transfer, including operation and destination, and enforces the request's format and custody. Spendability alone is not blanket authorization.

update-and-delete-custody-and-completion.text: Pending terminal requests keep their representative until valid completion, with no withdrawal, rejection or sweep. Completion consumes the request, burns the representative and applies the transition atomically. A completed request is never accepted again.

folding-and-actor-permissions.text: A fold applies requests against successive map states with absence and existing-value checks, recognizing authorization and explicit output requirements without a mandatory application callback. Singular imposes no owner, requester or folder gate; anyone may submit a satisfying transaction.

replay-and-reincarnation.text: One representative cannot sit in two pending terminal requests, and a consumed UTxO cannot be consumed again. Approval from a previous registration does not authorize a later incarnation outside its certified scope; the concrete fence is an open decision.

executing-witnesses-and-net-minting.text: The sequence diagram assigns a witness to each boundary: the application minting policy for action assets, the application spending validator for releases, Singular's spending witnesses for consuming requests, and the representative policy for supply coupling when a nonzero mint-field change invokes it.
Net quantities can cancel across Delete and reinsert, so the spending witnesses must enforce each logical transition; moving an existing token does not re-run its policy.

acceptance-scenarios.text: Twenty-one scenarios, none executed or proved, each with its required outcome and the governing sections named in the last column. They cover approved and unapproved Inserts, substitute policies, altered proposals, competing Inserts, Withdraw binding, local transitions, exact releases, custody escapes, completion of Update and Delete, reinsertion, replay, unrelated folders, outsider outputs, and net-zero minting.

illustrative-naming-demo-obligations.text: Seven demo obligations trace register, occupied-name refusal, resolve, resolve during a pending terminal request, resolve of absent or Over keys, address change, and refusal of forged state or unauthorized changes to their governing sections.

open-decisions.text: Seven named decisions remain: configuration binding, action encoding and token lifecycle, Withdraw economics, incarnation scope, batching, transaction shapes and libraries, and the naming profile. Each carries a constraint on its resolution.
